core_obligations: Show that an element which is a unit modulo a given stage is a unit in the limit (proof lines 2459-2463).
Deduce that the kernel ideal lies in the Jacobson radical (proof lines 2464-2466).
Take a monic polynomial with a factorisation of its reduction generating the unit ideal and lift it successively through the system (proof lines 2467-2473).
Verify at each step that the lifted factors generate the unit ideal, using that the spectra over two stages agree (proof lines 2474-2479).
proof_roadmap: Units and the Jacobson radical (proof lines 2459-2466).
Successive lifting of the factorisation (proof lines 2467-2473).
The unit ideal condition at each stage (proof lines 2474-2479).
difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that the inverse limit of a system of rings whose transition maps are surjective with locally nilpotent kernels, together with the kernel of the projection to any stage, is a henselian pair. The proof first checks that an element which is a unit modulo some stage is a unit in the limit, using the local nilpotence of the kernels, so that the ideal of the pair lies in the Jacobson radical. Then a monic polynomial with a factorisation of its reduction which generates the unit ideal is lifted factor by factor through the system, and at each stage the lifted factors are checked to generate the unit ideal by comparing the spectra of the polynomial rings over two stages, which are homeomorphic because the kernel is locally nilpotent.
